mainTopic: How רבי told רבי חייא to kill a bird without needing כיסוי הדם, and the משנה about שחיטה by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, with רבי מאיר's reason for being lenient
overview: The amud begins by finishing the story of רבי חייא's flax. רבי told him to kill a bird for its blood in a way that would not need כיסוי הדם. The גמרא explains why רב דימי's version ('צא טרוף') and רבין's version ('צא נחור') each mention only one method: each teaches a different חידוש in a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Next the גמרא asks how moths could harm רבי חייא's flax at all, since flax was protected in his merit. It answers that a צדיק's merit can help the world but not himself, like רבי חנינא בן דוסא. Then a new משנה rules on שחיטה done by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, for כיסוי הדם and for אותו ואת בנו. The גמרא concludes that the חכמים argue with רבי מאיר on both laws. It then asks why רבי מאיר is lenient: רבי אמי says it is because most of their actions are done wrong. The גמרא challenges why a majority is needed, since רבי מאיר worries even about a minority joined to a חזקה, and it begins proving this from the משנה of a child found next to dough. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רב דימי's version says only 'Go and make it a טרפה'
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי's version mentions 'צא טרוף' because it is the bigger חידוש. Of course נחירה is not שחיטה, but you might have thought an unfit שחיטה - slaughtering after the bird was made a טרפה - still counts as שחיטה and needs כיסוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking in a 'not needed' style. Of course נחירה, killing the bird without שחיטה, does not need covering, since that is not שחיטה at all. But with 'make it a טרפה' - first making the bird a טרפה and then slaughtering it - I might think an unfit שחיטה is still called שחיטה and needs covering. So he teaches us like רבי חייא בר אבא, that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of why רב דימי's version did not say 'צא נחור'. He chose the less obvious case to teach a bigger lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחירה, killing the bird without a valid שחיטה, is clearly not שחיטה, so it obviously needs no כיסוי. A bird that was first made a טרפה and then slaughtered looks more like real שחיטה, so you might think it needs כיסוי. By saying 'צא טרוף', רבי shows that even this unfit שחיטה is not counted as שחיטה for כיסוי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: He is speaking in a 'not needed' style: he states the bigger חידוש, and the easier case is understood on its own

Go out and do נחירה: kill the bird without שחיטה - Rashi (85b) explains נחירה as choking (נוחרו חונקו); others explain it as stabbing. It is not עקירה, ripping out the windpipe and gullet (Rashi there: עוקרו עוקר סימנים).
Go out and make it a טרפה: first make the bird a טרפה, then slaughter it, so that the act is a שחיטה שאינה ראויה (Rashi 85b: עשהו תחלה טרפה ואח"כ שחוט).
A שחיטה that is not fit, meaning it does not make the meat permitted
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal
It teaches us (this new point)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא מיבעיא' does not mean the obvious case is wrong or left out. It means the obvious case is already included, so the speaker mentions only the harder case.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רב דימי, whose version of the story said 'צא טרוף'.

phrases.english: It is not necessary to say 'Go out and do נחירה'
since that is not slaughter at all,
but with 'Go out and make it a טרפה', I might say
a slaughter that is not fit is still called slaughter
and it should need covering,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: so he teaches us like רבי חייא בר אבא.
phrases.notes: His teaching is quoted in step 3: רבי agreed with רבי שמעון about כיסוי הדם.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unfit שחיטה is still called שחיטה, so the blood would need covering.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unfit שחיטה is not called שחיטה for כיסוי הדם, following רבי חייא בר אבא.

steps.title: Why does רבין's version not say 'Go and make it a טרפה'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the same question about the other version: why did רבין's version say 'צא נחור' and not 'צא טרוף'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says 'Go out and do נחירה', why didn't he say 'Go out and make it a טרפה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second version of the story, רבין's, and asks why it uses נחירה and not the טרפה method. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that 'צא טרוף' is the bigger חידוש. So it seems strange that רבין's version would mention the simpler case of נחירה, killing without שחיטה. The גמרא wants to know what point that version is making.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'Go out and do נחירה',
what is the reason he did not say 'Go out and make it a טרפה'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר צֵא נְחוֹר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר צֵא טְרוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1: having explained רב דימי's version, the גמרא now questions רבין's version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבין's version has רבי choosing נחירה over a שחיטה done after the bird was made a טרפה.

steps.title: Blocking an easy answer: רבי holds an unfit שחיטה is not שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: You cannot answer that רבי holds an unfit שחיטה counts as שחיטה, because רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, said רבי agreed with רבי שמעון that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he holds an unfit שחיטה is called שחיטה, so 'צא טרוף' would need covering, that cannot be. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי saw that רבי שמעון was right about כיסוי הדם, and he wrote it in the משנה under the name 'the Sages'!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering its own question, the גמרא blocks one possible answer. It proves from a known teaching that רבי does not count an unfit שחיטה as שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might explain that רבין's version avoided 'צא טרוף' because רבי thinks that method would need כיסוי. But רבי published רבי שמעון's view in the משנה as the opinion of 'the Sages', which shows he agreed with it. So that explanation fails. Step 4 gives the real answer to the question from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: it brings up a possible answer, usually so it can be rejected
He holds (this opinion)
In the name of 'the Sages', which is how the משנה presents a view it accepts as the main ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows how רבי, who edited the משנה, could show which view he agreed with: he wrote it as the view of 'the Sages'.

phrases.english: And if you will say he holds
that a slaughter that is not fit is called slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: but didn't רבי חייא בר אבא say in the name of רבי יוחנן:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: רבי saw that the words of רבי שמעון were right
about covering the blood,
and taught it in the name of 'the Sages'!
phrases.notes: He means רבי put רבי שמעון's view into our משנה as the opinion of 'the Sages'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא קָסָבַר שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to step 2 so that the question stays strong.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible answer that רבי holds an unfit שחיטה counts as שחיטה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, shows that רבי agreed with רבי שמעון that an unfit שחיטה is not שחיטה for כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: Why רבין's version says 'צא נחור': נחירה is not a bird's שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבין's version also uses 'לא מיבעיא'. Of course a bird first made a טרפה and then slaughtered needs no כיסוי. But you might think a bird needs no Torah שחיטה, so נחירה would count as its שחיטה and need כיסוי. The פסוק 'כאשר צויתיך' teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: He too is speaking in a 'not needed' style. Of course 'make it a טרפה' - first making it a טרפה, then slaughtering - needs no covering, since an unfit שחיטה is not called שחיטה. But with 'do נחירה', I might say a bird needs no שחיטה from the Torah, so נחירה is its שחיטה and it should need covering. He teaches us 'as I have commanded you'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 2. רבין's version also teaches a bigger חידוש, just about a different point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that a bird needs no Torah שחיטה, and by that view נחירה would be a valid killing that needs כיסוי. By telling רבי חייא to do נחירה to the bird so that no כיסוי would be needed, רבי shows he holds that birds do need שחיטה from the Torah, learned from 'כאשר צויתיך'. So each version teaches a different חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird does not need שחיטה from the Torah (a view that רבי does not accept)

Killing a bird (or animal) without שחיטה. Rashi (85b) explains נחירה as choking (נוחרו חונקו); others explain it as stabbing. Either way it is not עקירה - ripping out the windpipe and gullet (Rashi there: עוקרו עוקר סימנים).
'As I have commanded you': the פסוק that shows שחיטה is a Torah requirement

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use 'לא מיבעיא'. רב דימי's 'צא טרוף' teaches that an unfit שחיטה is not שחיטה. רבין's 'צא נחור' teaches that a bird needs Torah שחיטה, so נחירה does not count as its שחיטה. In both cases, no כיסוי is needed.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
phrases.notes: Now 'he' is רבין, whose version said 'צא נחור'.

phrases.english: It is not necessary to say 'Go out and make it a טרפה',

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: since a slaughter that is not fit is not called slaughter,
but with 'Go out and do נחירה', I might say:
a bird does not need slaughter from the Torah,
so its נחירה is its slaughter,
and it should need covering,
so he teaches us 'as I have commanded you'.
phrases.notes: דברים 12:21. This פסוק teaches that a bird does need שחיטה, so נחירה is not its שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2 in a way that does not run into the problem raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the speaker stated the bigger חידוש, here about Torah שחיטה for birds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds need no Torah שחיטה, so נחירה counts as their שחיטה and the blood needs covering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds need שחיטה from the Torah ('כאשר צויתיך'), so נחירה is not שחיטה and needs no כיסוי.

steps.title: Could moths really have harmed רבי חייא's flax?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now questions the story itself. A known teaching says that since the exiles came up from בבל, flax was no longer stricken, and the Sages credited this to the merit of רבי חייא and his sons. So how could his own flax get moths?
steps.simpleTranslation: And did moths really get into his flax? But didn't רבין בר אבא say, and some say רבי אבין בר שבא said: From the time the exiles came up, meteors, earthquakes, storm winds and thunder stopped. Their wine did not sour and their flax was not stricken. And the Sages credited this to רבי חייא and his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the basic story. How could moths harm רבי חייא's flax, if flax was protected in his merit? Step 6 answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion so far assumed that moths got into רבי חייא's flax. But the quoted teaching says flax stopped being stricken after the exiles came up, and the Sages linked this to רבי חייא and his sons. That seems to contradict the story itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Moths (or a similar pest) that damage flax
Flax (in the text it appears as בְּכִיתָּנֵיהּ, 'in his flax')
The people of the exile who came up from בבל to ארץ ישראל
Meteors or shooting stars
Earthquakes
Literally 'set their eyes on': they credited it to

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not continue the כיסוי הדם discussion. It is a new question about whether the story could have happened at all.

phrases.english: And did moths really get into his flax?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the story told earlier about רבי חייא's flax.

phrases.english: But didn't רבין בר אבא say,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר שְׁבָא:
phrases.english: and some say רבי אבין בר שבא said:
From when the people of the exile came up
the meteors and the earthquakes stopped
and the storm winds and the thunders,
and their wine did not turn sour,
and their flax was not stricken,
and the Sages set their eyes
on רבי חייא and his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the כיסוי הדם discussion and questions the basic facts of the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that moths got into רבי חייא's flax.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known teaching says flax stopped being stricken after the exiles came up, in the merit of רבי חייא and his sons. So his own flax should not have been harmed.

steps.title: Their merit helps the world, not themselves
steps.stepSummary: The merit of רבי חייא and his sons protects everyone else's flax, but not their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: When their merit works, it works for the world, but not for their own things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. The merit of רבי חייא and his sons protects the world's flax, but it does not protect their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that if their merit saved all flax, it must have saved their own flax too. The answer separates the two: a צדיק's merit can benefit others without benefiting himself. So there is no contradiction with the story of his flax getting moths.

keyTerms.meaning: their merit
the world (everyone else)
their own (things)

phrases.english: When their merit is effective,
it is for the world; for their own – not,
phrases.notes: "Their own" means their own flax, so the moths in רבי חייא's flax fit fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the earlier statement: the merit protects others only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their merit would protect their own flax too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their merit protects the world's flax, not their own.

steps.title: Proof from חנינא בן דוסא living on carobs
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול says the whole world is fed because of חנינא, yet he himself lives on a קב of carobs a week.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Every day a heavenly voice goes out and says: The whole world is fed because of My son חנינא, and My son חנינא is satisfied with one קב of carobs from one Friday to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that a צדיק's merit can help others but not himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's merit, the whole world has food. Yet he himself had almost nothing to eat. This is the same pattern as רבי חייא's flax.

keyTerms.meaning: a heavenly voice
a small measure of volume
carobs, a cheap and plain food
Friday, the day before שבת

steps.whatToRemember: A צדיק's merit can sustain the whole world while he himself lives with very little.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
for Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת וְאוֹמֶרֶת:
phrases.english: Each and every day a heavenly voice goes out and says:
The entire world is fed
because of Chanina, My son,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חָרוּבִין
phrases.english: and for Chanina, My son, a kav of carobs is enough
from one Shabbat eve to the next Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a צדיק's merit can help others without helping himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בת קול about רבי חנינא בן דוסא, quoted by רב יהודה in the name of רב.

steps.title: משנה: Covering the blood after שחיטה by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן
steps.stepSummary: If others watched their שחיטה, the blood must be covered. If they slaughtered alone, there is no obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן who slaughtered while others watched them: one must cover the blood. If they slaughtered by themselves, one is exempt from covering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on כיסוי הדם when people who cannot be trusted on their own perform שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With someone watching, we know the שחיטה was done properly, so it is a real שחיטה and the blood must be covered. With no one watching, we cannot rely on it, so there is no obligation to cover the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, the משנה
a deaf-mute
a person who is not mentally competent
a minor
by themselves, with no one watching

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor who slaughtered,
and others were watching them –
one is obligated to cover the blood.
If by themselves – one is exempt from covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supervised שחיטה by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן requires כיסוי הדם. Unsupervised שחיטה does not.

steps.title: משנה: The same people and אותו ואת בנו
steps.stepSummary: If others watched, one may not slaughter the offspring the same day. If no one watched, רבי מאיר permits it and חכמים forbid it, but they agree there are no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to אותו ואת בנו. If they slaughtered while others watched, one may not slaughter the offspring after them. If they slaughtered by themselves, רבי מאיר permits slaughtering after them and חכמים forbid it. חכמים agree that if one did slaughter, he does not get the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same people to the איסור of slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day. In the unsupervised case there is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Supervised שחיטה counts, so the offspring is forbidden. For unsupervised שחיטה, רבי מאיר says it does not count, so the offspring is permitted. חכמים forbid the offspring, yet they agree there are no lashes, since maybe the mother's שחיטה was not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: the איסור of slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
they agree
receives the forty lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים forbid slaughtering the offspring, but they do not say it is a definite Torah sin. That is why there are no lashes.

phrases.english: And likewise regarding a mother and its offspring,
if they slaughtered and others were watching them –
phrases.notes: "They" are the same חרש, שוטה, and קטן, slaughtering the mother animal.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to slaughter after them,
if by themselves –
Rabbi Meir permits slaughtering after them,
and the Sages forbid,
and they agree that if one did slaughter –
he does not receive the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving to a second area of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supervised שחיטה forbids the offspring that day. Unsupervised: רבי מאיר permits, חכמים forbid, and there are no lashes.

steps.title: Why do חכמים agree in the first case but argue in the second?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים seem to treat unsupervised שחיטה as invalid for כיסוי but as valid for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And according to חכמים, why is the first case different, where they do not argue, and why is the last case different, where they do argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by pointing out an apparent contradiction in חכמים' view. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, nobody argues that unsupervised שחיטה needs no כיסוי, which suggests it does not count as שחיטה. Yet for אותו ואת בנו, חכמים forbid the offspring, which suggests it does count. The גמרא wants to know why חכמים switch.

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause of the משנה
the last clause of the משנה
what is the difference?
they disagree

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis – what is different about the first clause, where they do not disagree,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the כיסוי case, where חכמים let the "exempt" ruling stand.

phrases.english: and what is different about the last clause, where they do disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of חכמים' position in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Silence in the רישא implies unsupervised שחיטה is not שחיטה. Forbidding the offspring in the סיפא implies it is. Both cannot be true without some explanation.

steps.title: Covering the blood could make people think the meat is kosher
steps.stepSummary: חכמים do not require כיסוי in the רישא because people would then assume the unsupervised שחיטה was valid and come to eat the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first case, if we required them to cover the blood, people would say the slaughter is proper, and they would come to eat from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. חכמים are not really calling the שחיטה invalid. They skip כיסוי so that people will not think the meat is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים are unsure whether unsupervised שחיטה is valid. So they forbid the offspring in case the שחיטה was valid. The exemption from כיסוי is not a ruling that the שחיטה is invalid. It is a protective measure against people wrongly eating the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה (here, the case of covering the blood)
A proper, valid slaughter
To cover the blood (כיסוי הדם)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as חכמים saying the שחיטה is definitely invalid. They are unsure, and they exempt כיסוי only so people won't mistakenly eat the meat.

phrases.english: In the first clause, if we say they are obligated to cover,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where a חרש, שוטה or קטן slaughtered with nobody watching.

phrases.english: people will say: it is a proper slaughter,
and they will come to eat from their slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic protective measure: the ruling is driven by fear of a mistaken conclusion, not by the validity of the שחיטה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים view unsupervised שחיטה as invalid for כיסוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים are unsure about its validity. They exempt כיסוי only so people will not think the meat is kosher.

steps.title: The same worry should apply to the offspring case
steps.stepSummary: If forbidding the offspring also signals a valid שחיטה, the same fear should stop חכמים from forbidding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the latter clause too: since the Rabbis say it is forbidden to slaughter the offspring after them, people will say the slaughter was proper and come to eat from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 11. Forbidding the slaughter of the offspring could also make people think the mother's שחיטה counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of step 11 was to avoid any ruling that suggests the שחיטה was valid. Forbidding the offspring under אותו ואת בנו also seems to treat the mother's שחיטה as a real one. So the same worry should apply here too.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה (here, the case of אותו ואת בנו)
After them, meaning slaughtering the offspring after these people slaughtered the mother

phrases.english: The latter clause too:
since the Rabbis say
it is forbidden to slaughter after them,
phrases.notes: This means slaughtering the offspring on the same day the mother was slaughtered (אותו ואת בנו).

phrases.english: people will say: it is a proper slaughter,
and they will come to eat from their slaughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 11 by applying it to the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The protective reasoning given in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If fear of a mistaken conclusion cancels כיסוי, it should also cancel the ban on slaughtering the offspring, since that ban suggests the same mistake.

steps.title: People will assume the owner did not need the meat
steps.stepSummary: Holding back from slaughtering the offspring does not suggest anything about the mother's שחיטה. People will just think the owner did not need more meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the latter clause, people will say: it is meat he does not need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 12. When people see the owner not slaughtering the offspring, they will think he did not want more meat. They will not think the mother's שחיטה was valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not doing something gives no clear message, because there are plenty of everyday reasons not to slaughter an animal. So the stringency in the סיפא carries no risk of people learning the wrong thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat
He does not need it

phrases.english: In the latter clause, people will say:
it is meat that he does not need.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא, אָמְרִי: בִּשְׂרָא דְּלָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: refraining has an innocent explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding the offspring signals the mother's שחיטה was valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Observers will assume the owner simply did not need the meat.

steps.title: Covering the blood could look like cleaning the yard
steps.stepSummary: The same kind of innocent explanation should work for כיסוי too: people will think he is just cleaning his courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause too, people will say: he needs to clean his courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer of step 13 back onto the רישא. If people can find an innocent reason for not slaughtering, they can also find one for covering blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering blood can easily look like simple tidying up. If so, requiring כיסוי would not suggest the שחיטה was valid, and חכמים should require it.

keyTerms.meaning: To clean out, to clear
His courtyard

phrases.english: In the first clause too, people will say:
he needs to clean his courtyard!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא נָמֵי, אָמְרִי: לְנַקֵּר חֲצֵירוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 13 to challenge step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exemption from כיסוי explained in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Covering blood has an innocent explanation too (cleaning the yard), so there is no real risk of a mistaken conclusion, and כיסוי should be required.

steps.title: Cases where the cleaning excuse does not work
steps.stepSummary: In a garbage dump nobody cleans, and someone who asks בית דין gets a direct ruling. In these cases a requirement to cover would clearly signal a valid שחיטה, so חכמים exempt כיסוי in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered in a garbage dump, what can be said? If one comes to consult, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 14. The 'cleaning the yard' excuse does not work in every situation, so the exemption from כיסוי stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody covers blood in a garbage dump to keep it clean. And if a person asks בית דין and is told to cover, he will conclude the שחיטה was valid. Because some cases carry this real risk, חכמים exempt כיסוי for all unsupervised שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A garbage dump
To consult, to ask for a ruling (from בית דין)
What can be said? (there is no good answer)

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a passing stage. Here the גמרא says חכמים exempt כיסוי because covering in a dump, or after asking בית דין, could suggest the meat is kosher. But step 16 attacks this answer, and in step 17 the גמרא drops it: חכמים actually require כיסוי.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered in a garbage dump,
what can be said?
phrases.notes: Nobody cleans a garbage dump, so the 'cleaning the yard' excuse doesn't work there.

phrases.english: If one comes to consult,
phrases.notes: Someone comes to ask בית דין whether he has to cover the blood.

phrases.english: what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and confirms the reasoning of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing cases where the innocent explanation fails, which justifies a blanket rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering can always be explained as cleaning the yard, so כיסוי should be required.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a dump, or when someone asks בית דין, covering would signal a valid שחיטה, so חכמים exempt כיסוי across the board.

steps.title: The same problem returns for someone who asks about the offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the last answer against itself. If asking בית דין gets a direct ruling that reveals the שחיטה was valid, the same thing happens when someone asks about slaughtering the offspring in the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your own reasoning, the latter clause has the same problem: if someone comes to ask בית דין, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 15. That answer said a ruling from בית דין clearly shows the שחיטה was valid. The same should be true when the question is about the offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the גמרא said that a person who asks בית דין gets a direct ruling, so a requirement to cover would look like an approval of the שחיטה. But someone can also ask בית דין, 'May I slaughter the offspring today?' If בית דין says no, he will think the mother's שחיטה was valid. So by this logic the חכמים should not forbid the offspring either.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: turning the other side's logic back against them
The latter clause of the משנה, here the law of slaughtering the offspring (אותו ואת בנו)
Comes to consult, meaning he asks בית דין for a ruling

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning, the latter clause as well,
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the law about slaughtering the offspring on the same day.

phrases.english: if he comes to consult the court –
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'asks בית דין' case from step 15 to undo the step 13 difference between כיסוי and the offspring.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חכמים exempt כיסוי in every case but still forbid the offspring
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A direct ruling from בית דין that forbids the offspring would signal a valid שחיטה just as much as a ruling that requires כיסוי. So the difference between the two laws falls apart.

steps.title: The חכמים argue on both laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier reading. The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about כיסוי too. They waited until he finished his whole statement and then argued on all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the חכמים disagree about the whole matter. They waited for רבי מאיר until he finished his statement, and then they argued against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the idea that the חכמים agree to exempt כיסוי. Instead, it says the חכמים argue on both laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only shows the חכמים disagreeing at the end, in the offspring case. The גמרא explains that this is just about timing: they let רבי מאיר finish and then argued. So for the חכמים, an unsupervised שחיטה by these people requires כיסוי and forbids the offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about the whole matter, both laws
They waited
Against him, about what he said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as if the חכמים argue only on the offspring because that is the only place their name appears. According to this answer, their argument covers כיסוי as well.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the whole משנה. The two opinions now run straight across both laws: רבי מאיר is lenient on both, and the חכמים are strict on both.

phrases.english: Rather, the Rabbis disagree about the entire matter,
phrases.notes: This means the כיסוי law in the first clause too, not only the offspring.

phrases.english: and they waited for Rabbi Meir
until he finished his statement,
and then they disagreed with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 16 and gives the משנה a new reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה: the disagreement covers both clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that no כיסוי is needed and argue only about the offspring.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים require כיסוי and forbid the offspring. They waited for רבי מאיר to finish and then argued on everything.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason for being lenient?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים's view makes sense, because they are strict out of doubt. But why is רבי מאיר lenient on both laws when the שחיטה might have been valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the חכמים rule strictly. But what is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the two opinions are clear, the גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's reason. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are strict because maybe the שחיטה was done properly, so they require כיסוי and forbid the offspring. You would expect רבי מאיר to worry about the same doubt. The גמרא wants to know why he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable: grants one side before asking about the other
To be strict

phrases.english: Granted, the Rabbis rule stringently,
but Rabbi Meir – what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why רבי מאיר does not worry that the שחיטה might have been valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּנַן לְחוּמְרָא, אֶלָּא רַבִּי מֵאִיר – מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both opinions are fixed, asks for רבי מאיר's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר is lenient on both כיסוי and the offspring even though the שחיטה might have been valid

steps.title: For רבי מאיר, their שחיטה is plain נבלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי מאיר gives lashes for eating from the שחיטה of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, because it counts as נבלה. For him there is no doubt at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר used to hold a person liable for eating from their שחיטה, because it is נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי מאיר is not unsure. He treats their unsupervised שחיטה as definitely not a שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are only given for a sure sin, so רבי מאיר must hold that the meat is surely נבלה. If the שחיטה is surely invalid, there is no reason to cover the blood or to forbid the offspring. That is why he is lenient on both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds a person liable, here to lashes
Their slaughter, the שחיטה done by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה; eating it is forbidden by the תורה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Meir would hold one liable
for their slaughter, on account of an animal carcass.
phrases.notes: Liable means lashes for eating the meat. 'Their' means the חרש, שוטה, and קטן from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מְחַיֵּיב הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי מאיר, the unsupervised שחיטה of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is surely נבלה, and eating it brings lashes. With no doubt, there is no reason to be strict.

steps.title: Why they are presumed to fail: most of their actions are done wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's certainty. רבי אמי answers that most actions of a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are done wrong, so we follow the majority and assume their שחיטה was done wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? רבי אמי said: since most of their actions are done wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר is so sure the שחיטה was invalid. רבי אמי explains that we follow the majority: most of what these people do is done wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר uses a רוב, a majority. Since most of their actions are done wrong, we treat this שחיטה as done wrong too. So it counts as surely נבלה, which explains the lashes and the leniency about כיסוי and the offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
Majority: following what usually happens
Spoiled, done wrong

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר on both laws: they require כיסוי and forbid the offspring, because the שחיטה may have been valid. רבי מאיר is lenient on both because he treats the שחיטה of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן as surely נבלה, and eating it even brings lashes. רבי אמי bases this on a רוב, and the next step questions that reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation sets up the next challenge. Elsewhere רבי מאיר is known to worry about a מיעוט, so the next step asks why רבי אמי needed a רוב at all.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Rabbi Ami said:
Since the majority of their actions are bungled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הוֹאִיל וְרוֹב מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן מְקוּלְקָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's report in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most actions of a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are done wrong, so their שחיטה is treated as invalid based on the majority.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר need a majority at all?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) challenges רבי אמי's explanation. רבי מאיר takes a minority seriously when it joins with a חזקה, so even a minority of bad שחיטות should be enough to make the animal נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רב הונא son of רב יהושע (some say it was the other way around): Why did רבי אמי say specifically that 'most' of their actions are done wrong? Even if only a minority were done wrong, it should be the same. רבי מאיר worries about a minority, so join that minority to the animal's starting status (forbidden while alive), and the majority loses its strength.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's reason from step 20. It argues that רבי מאיר would not even need a majority of bad actions to rule this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said that רבי מאיר follows the רוב, meaning most actions of a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are done wrong. The challenge says this reason is more than רבי מאיר needs. He is known to be concerned for a מיעוט when it joins a חזקה, and a living animal has a חזקה of being forbidden. So even if most of their שחיטות were good, the minority of bad ones plus that חזקה would cancel out the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? A way of asking why a narrow reason was given when a broader one would also work
A minority
A presumed status: we assume things stay as they were until we know otherwise
The majority is weakened, so it can no longer decide the case on its own

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this question argues against רבי מאיר's ruling. It agrees with the ruling and only says that רבי אמי's reason, a majority, is more than רבי מאיר needs.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said
to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: and some say that Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
said to Rav Pappa:
Why specifically a majority?
phrases.notes: He is asking about רבי אמי's reason, that most of their actions are done wrong.

phrases.english: Even a minority would also be enough,
since Rabbi Meir is concerned for a minority.
Join the minority to the presumptive status,
phrases.notes: The חזקה here is that an animal is forbidden to eat while it is alive, until a valid שחיטה is done.

phrases.english: and the majority is weakened.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא רוֹב? אֲפִילּוּ מִיעוּט נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי אמי gave in step 20 as more than רבי מאיר needs
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's explanation that רבי מאיר's ruling rests on a majority of bungled actions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר is concerned for a מיעוט that joins a חזקה. The animal's חזקה of being forbidden plus a minority of bad שחיטות would already weaken the majority, so there is no need to say most of their actions are done wrong.

steps.title: Proof: the child found next to the dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that רבי מאיר is concerned for a minority. In the case of a child found next to pure dough with a piece of dough in his hand, רבי מאיר rules the dough pure and the חכמים rule it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a child is found next to dough and has a piece of dough in his hand. רבי מאיר says the dough is pure. The חכמים say it is impure, because children usually handle things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving its claim from step 21 that רבי מאיר worries about a minority. It quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about a child and some dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child is impure, and the question is whether he touched the pure dough. The חכמים say he did, since children normally touch things. רבי מאיר rules the dough pure even though children normally touch things. The next step explains how that shows he relies on a minority.

keyTerms.meaning: A small child
A batch of dough that has been started
A piece of dough
To handle or touch things with the hands

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: טהרות 3:8.

phrases.english: A child who is found next to the started dough
with a piece of dough in his hand,
phrases.notes: The child is impure, and the dough is pure. The question is whether he touched it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir deems the dough pure,
and the Rabbis deem it impure,
because it is the way of a child to handle things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up step 21's claim that רבי מאיר is concerned for a minority
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר takes a minority seriously when it joins a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in טהרות 3:8 about the child found next to the dough

steps.title: רבי מאיר joins the minority to the dough's purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier explanation of רבי מאיר in that משנה. Most children handle things and a minority do not, but the dough has a חזקה of purity, and רבי מאיר joins the minority to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said about this: What is רבי מאיר's reason? He holds that most children handle things and a minority do not, and this dough stands in its presumption of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the dough משנה proves its point. רבי מאיר rules the dough pure even though most children touch things. The explanation is still being completed and continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority points toward impurity, since most children touch things. Two things stand against it: the minority of children who do not touch, and the dough's חזקה of being pure. רבי מאיר puts those two together against the majority, which is exactly what step 21 wants to do with the animal's חזקה of being forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his view
A majority
A presumption of purity, since the dough was pure before

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the model for the argument in step 21. If רבי מאיר lets a minority plus a חזקה overcome a majority here, he should do the same with a minority of bad שחיטות plus the חזקה of a living animal being forbidden.

phrases.english: And we said about this mishna:
What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir?
He holds that most children handle things,
and a minority do not handle things,
and this dough stands in its presumption of purity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from step 22 so that it can serve as proof for step 21
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר joins a minority to a חזקה to weaken a majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גמרא's earlier explanation of רבי מאיר's reason in the dough משנה
